Now let's talk about the Western Empire. Because that’s where our focus will be for the rest of the semester. In 476, the Goths destroy Rome. Why? Because power had shifted from the empire to the Catholic Church. The empire no longer has much power and recruits mercenaries who can’t be paid, leading them to sack Rome.

By this time, Rome is no longer a significant power. Augustine, the main architect of the Catholic Church, takes Paul's ideas and systemizes them. He teaches in "The City of God" that the Catholic Church is beyond history, divine, deciding who goes to heaven and who burns in hell, giving it immense power.

Europe has many geographic barriers, allowing diversity among its countries historically because unification was hard due to geography. This leads to innovation through conflict. When the Western Roman Empire falls, many groups fight for what remains.

When we say the Roman Empire rises and falls, our understanding differs from theirs; they believe their warlords are the empire now. Eventually, this leads to the rise of a new power: the Franks. The Franks see themselves as the heirs of Rome, needing legitimacy from the Catholic Church. In about 800, Charlemagne, king of the Franks, is crowned Holy Roman Emperor by the Pope.

From then on, it's the Catholic Church and the Pope who decide the Holy Roman Empire’s leadership. The church becomes wealthy due to this power and anoints the Holy Roman Empire. This is Charlemagne, buried in Aachen Cathedral, one of the most beautiful buildings in the world; his body still lies there.
